performance_finding: Cross-process central batching is correct and observable but 4.60-6.85x slower than per-driver servers on the wall measure (5.70/1.24 and 7.19/1.05) and 7.64-10.22x slower on the per-driver steady mean (6.19/0.81 and 3.27/0.32), with the same batching policy and model in both. Per-match encode and staged forward time both rise, so transport and service/CPU contention are not isolated. Reported for P6/P7 transport selection, not as a model-compute conclusion.
provenance_note: All performance rows were measured at commit 5c9096a by the committed docs/phases/P3/evidence/run_baseline.py (sha256 in evidence_sha256). Each run's full report, run_config and stage timings are retained as evidence/baseline_<run_id>.json; aggregate and per-driver stage seconds are in BASELINE_STAGE_TIMING.csv.
optimisations: batched decode: one observe_fixed_batch for all requesting seats instead of 2*N calls
collector reuses the env's already-decoded observations instead of decoding twice
request_info_batch for all rows/seats in one call
staged inference: all ENCODEs, then all STEP rows per level, submitted together
defects_found_and_fixed: ProcessInferenceServer.client() caches one client, so [srv.client() for _ in range(n)] produced n references to slot 0 and every forward was B=1; srv.clients(n) returns distinct slots
per-request branch count was not tracked, so completed requests kept requesting further levels
batched decode initially mishandled layout-derived role/side ids
the fallback decode path lacked role_ids/side_ids entirely
mp daemonic processes cannot spawn an inference server; drivers must be non-daemonic
G3-C's truncation-exclusion test compared an expression with itself and could never fail; accounting extracted into account_step() and unit-tested
match ids carried a hardcoded worker 0; the driver index is now carried
the two-seat claim only asserted a nonzero total; decisions are counted per seat and both must be nonzero
G3-D lacked cross-worker and mixed-version controls; both added
PERFORMANCE_BASELINE.csv labelled multi-driver rows with a commit where multi_driver.py did not exist; regenerated with the tested commit
the receipt paired an accumulation-sweep batch mean with a different run's throughput; the sweep was removed and the baseline regenerated
P3-C transition retention was absent; BoundedTransitionStore + PA4ActorTransitionV1 records implemented and tested
'central' inference was per-driver; a single distributed-transport server now serves spawned drivers, proven by per-forward run-id sets
no weight fingerprint was stamped; sha256 fingerprint computed, stamped on responses and validated
duplicate identity inside one transport batch overwrote silently; now rejected
no independent lost-completion guard; ledger is compared with env.completed_matches
revised decisions were counted as behaviour rows; now excluded
limitations: AsyncBatchedCollector is not used; G3-A is a scoped PASS under ADR-008
central cross-process inference is 4.60-6.85x slower on the wall measure and 7.64-10.22x on the per-driver steady mean; transport vs service/CPU contention was not isolated
throughput ~7.2 matches/s on the wall measure (~9.7 steady matches/s for one driver), far below the 1,000/s stretch goal which the design forbids proving on this GPU
baseline runs use one seed per configuration and were run once; run-to-run variance is not characterised
GPU encode/step are nearly flat in batch size; wider batches do not by themselves increase throughput
random PA3 weights (seed 20261006); no strength or weight-parity claim
path B (staged prefix) only; path A would remove sequential level round-trips but is out of scope
transitions are in-memory and bounded; no replay database. Drops are counted, not silent
the distributed transport emits benign gloo shutdown warnings when drivers exit
same-model review is a process control, not independent model proof
